setup: Stand side-on to a solid wall
Far enough away for the ball to come back
Feet wider than hips, knees soft
Ball at hip height on the back side
execution: Turn hips first, then chest, then arms
Throw the ball hard into the wall
Catch it and reset before the next throw
faults: Don't throw with your arms alone
Don't twist from your lower back

notes: Throw only at a wall built for it, such as a solid concrete or padded wall, never at glass, mirrors or plasterboard. Check the area is clear.
Use a soft, light medicine ball (about 2–5 kg) so speed stays high and the rebound is easy to catch.
Each throw is a maximal effort. Keep sets short and rest fully.
If pain lingers or comes back, stop this exercise and get it checked by a physio or doctor.
stopIf: Pain in the lower back or side that builds
Pain that changes how you move

regressions.name: Half-kneeling rotational throw
regressions.reason: Kneeling removes the legs, so the trunk turn is easier to learn.

regressions.name: Lighter ball, slower throws
regressions.reason: Groove the hips-first order before adding speed.

progressions.name: Step-in rotational throw
progressions.reason: A step toward the wall adds more drive from the legs.

substitutions.name: Cable woodchop
substitutions.reason: Controlled rotation on a cable when no throwing wall is available.

substitutions.name: Pallof press
substitutions.reason: Trains the trunk to resist rotation instead.

substitutions.name: Medicine ball slam
substitutions.reason: Medicine-ball power work with no wall needed.

guideBrief.cameraNote: Front view at hip height, figure side-on to a wall on the right of the frame, so the hip and chest turn toward the wall and the ball's flight are clear.

keyPositions.label: Load
keyPositions.describe: Feet wider than hips, knees soft. Hips and chest turned away from the wall, weight on the back leg, ball held at hip height on the back side with both hands.

keyPositions.label: Release
keyPositions.describe: Hips have turned toward the wall first, chest following, arms swinging through. Back heel lifted and pivoting on the ball of the foot. Ball leaving the hands toward the wall.

keyPositions.label: Catch
keyPositions.describe: Facing the wall side-on again, catching the rebound at hip height and turning back into the load position.

ikHints: Back foot pivots on the ball of the foot during the throw
emphasise: Hips turn first, then chest, then arms
Ball thrown hard to the wall
